The nanoindentation hardness values (19Al hardest sample H_Ave = 10.4 ± 1.3 GPa), the intrinsic β-Mn hardness (19Al = 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa), the SEM-EDS β-Mn composition of the hardest 19Al sample (Mn 36.2 at.%, Al 17.5 at.%, Cu 2.6 at.%) and the fracture toughness KIC (19Al = 3.5 MPa·m1/2) reported in the paper were all measured on the hardest state of the 19Al alloy (600 °C/10 h, 917.8 HV), not on the 19Al 550 °C/6 h sample, so they are not attributed to this sample.

The interphase new BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates at β-Mn interfaces are documented for the ultra-hard (fully transformed) states, e.g. 19Al at 600 °C/3 h and 650 °C/6 h (Fig. 6), rather than for the partially transformed 19Al 550 °C/6 h sample.
